items.followUp: Find the volume of 300 g of copper having density 8900 kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: The mass must be converted to SI units before using the density formula.
rubric.description: Converts the mass to kilograms.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the mass as 0.2 kg.

rubric.why: The volume follows from mass divided by density.
rubric.description: Uses the density relation and obtains the volume with a correct unit.
rubric.how: Award for the correct calculation and volume in m³.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 200 g = 0.2 kg, ρ = 11300 kg m⁻³
Formula: ρ = m/V, so V = m/ρ
Substitution: V = 0.2 kg ÷ 11300 kg m⁻³

rubric.why: The Celsius-to-kelvin conversion requires adding 273.
rubric.description: States or applies the Celsius-to-kelvin relation.
rubric.how: Award for K = °C + 273.

rubric.why: Adding 273 to 20 gives 293.
rubric.description: Gives the converted temperature with its unit.
rubric.how: Award for 293 K.

modelAnswer: Formula: T(K) = T(°C) + 273
Substitution: T = 20 + 273

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The derivation begins with a velocity-time graph showing initial and final velocities.
rubric.description: Identifies the graph and its endpoint velocities.
rubric.how: Award for a correctly labelled velocity-time graph or a clear description of it.

rubric.why: The area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement.
rubric.description: Relates the area under the graph to displacement.
rubric.how: Award for stating this graph property.

rubric.why: The area is the rectangle plus the triangle, using acceleration for the change in velocity.
rubric.description: Finds displacement as rectangle area plus triangle area.
rubric.how: Award for a correct area expression.

rubric.why: Substituting v − u = at gives the first equation of motion in displacement form.
rubric.description: Obtains the first equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award for s = ut + ½at².

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with time on the horizontal axis and velocity on the vertical axis; the velocity changes from u at t = 0 to v at time t.
Displacement s is the area under the velocity-time graph.
Area = rectangle + triangle: s = ut + ½(v − u)t
Acceleration a = (v − u)/t, so v − u = at.
Therefore, s = ut + ½at² (the first equation of motion).

items.followUp: Explain how a force of 20 N acting at 30° to the horizontal can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Resolution means replacing a force with component forces.
rubric.description: States what resolution of forces is.
rubric.how: Award for defining resolution as splitting or replacing a force by components.

rubric.why: The components together must have the same effect as the original force.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship between the components and original force.
rubric.how: Award for stating that their resultant equals the original force.

rubric.why: A force is resolved along chosen directions, commonly perpendicular axes.
rubric.description: Identifies the chosen directions of the components.
rubric.how: Award for perpendicular components or components along specified axes.

rubric.why: For θ measured from the horizontal, these are the horizontal and vertical components.
rubric.description: Gives the component relations for perpendicular axes.
rubric.how: Award for the correct sine and cosine component expressions.

modelAnswer: Resolution of forces is the process of splitting a force into two or more component forces in specified directions.
The component forces together produce the same effect as the original force; their vector sum equals that force.
For a force F at angle θ to the horizontal, resolve it into perpendicular horizontal and vertical components.
Horizontal component: Fₓ = F cos θ; vertical component: Fᵧ = F sin θ.

items.followUp: A 2 kg ball is thrown vertically upwards at 10 m s⁻¹. Find its maximum potential energy and its kinetic energy just before it returns to the ground. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The mass must be expressed in kilograms, and the initial velocity and gravitational acceleration identified.
rubric.description: Records the relevant data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for m = 0.5 kg and u = 15 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: At maximum height the final velocity is zero, giving a maximum height of 11.25 m when g = 10 m s⁻².
rubric.description: Finds the maximum height correctly.
rubric.how: Award for using the vertical motion relation and obtaining h = 11.25 m.

rubric.why: Potential energy at the maximum height is mgh.
rubric.description: Calculates maximum potential energy.
rubric.how: Award for PE = 56.25 J.

rubric.why: The stone’s initial kinetic energy is converted to potential energy at the top and regained on returning to the ground, neglecting air resistance.
rubric.description: Uses conservation of mechanical energy for the return to the ground.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the ground-level kinetic energy as equal to the initial kinetic energy.

rubric.why: The calculated kinetic energy on hitting the ground is 56.25 J.
rubric.description: States the kinetic energy when the stone hits the ground.
rubric.how: Award for the correct value with joules.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 500 g = 0.5 kg, u = 15 m s⁻¹, g = 10 m s⁻²
At maximum height, v = 0; use v² = u² + 2as with a = −g.
Substitution: 0 = 15² − 2(10)h, so h = 11.25 m
(i) P.E. at maximum height = mgh = 0.5 × 10 × 11.25 = 56.25 J
(ii) Neglecting air resistance, the stone returns to the ground with its initial kinetic energy.
K.E. on hitting the ground = ½mu² = ½ × 0.5 × 15² = 56.25 J

items.followUp: What is the least count of a micrometer screw gauge, and how is it determined?

rubric.why: Least count is the smallest measurement an instrument can measure accurately.
rubric.description: Defines least count.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as the smallest measurable value.

accept: least count = 1 MSD/number of vernier divisions
rubric.why: For vernier callipers, least count is determined from the main-scale and vernier-scale divisions.
rubric.description: Explains how the least count of vernier callipers is determined.
rubric.how: Award for the difference between one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division, or the equivalent calculation.

modelAnswer: The least count of vernier callipers is the smallest length that can be measured accurately with them.
It is determined by finding the difference between one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division: L.C. = 1 MSD − 1 VSD.

rubric.why: Nuclear physics concerns the atomic nucleus and its properties or reactions.
rubric.description: Describes nuclear physics.
rubric.how: Award for linking nuclear physics with the nucleus or nuclear reactions.

rubric.why: Atomic physics concerns the structure and properties of atoms, including their electrons.
rubric.description: Describes atomic physics.
rubric.how: Award for linking atomic physics with atoms, their structure, or their electrons.

modelAnswer: Nuclear physics is the branch of physics that studies the properties and behaviour of atomic nuclei and nuclear reactions.
Atomic physics is the branch of physics that studies the structure and properties of atoms, including their electrons.
